Rashi on Gittin 55b:10:1.hebrew: לקח מן האיש - קרקע המיוחדת לכתובת אשתו, או שכתוב בכתובתה, או הכניסתו לו שום בכתובתה, וכל שכן שאר נכסים, דאי לא עבדה ליה, אמר לה: "עיניך נתת בגרושין ובמיתה". הכי מוקמינן ליה בב"ב (נ.):
Rashi on Gittin 55b:10:1.english: If one purchased from the husband - [This refers to] land designated for his wife's ketubah, or [land] that is written in her ketubah, or [land] that she brought to him as an appraised [property] in her ketubah — and all the more so [to his] other properties — for if she had not done [so] for him, he would say to her, "You have set your eyes on divorce or [my] death!" Thus we establish it in Bava Batra (50a):

Rashi on Gittin 55b:10:2.english: His purchase is void - because she [can] say, "I [only] acted to please my husband":

Rashi on Gittin 55b:11:1.hebrew: נותן לבעלים רביע - ששיערו דסיקריקון מוזיל גבי' ריבעא:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:11:1.english: He gives the owners a fourth - for they estimated that the Sicarius discounts [the price] for him by a fourth:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:14:1.hebrew: לא דנו דין סיקריקון - בהרוגי המלחמה, דקני הסיקריקון לגמרי והלוקח ממנו מקחו קיים, אבל מהרוגי המלחמה ואילך, הלוקח ממנו יש לו דין המפורש במשנתינו:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:14:1.english: They did not apply the law of Sicarii - during [the time of] those killed in the war, for [the Sicarius] acquires [the property] completely and [for] one who buys from him, his purchase stands; however, from [the time of] those killed in the war and onward, one who buys from him is subject to the law explained in our Mishnah:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:14:2.english: For Rabbi Asi said, he issued three decrees - Titus, in his war:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:14:3.hebrew: כל דלא קטיל - ישראל, כל היכא דמשכח ליה:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:14:3.english: Anyone who does not kill - a Jew, wherever he finds him:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:14:4.hebrew: לקטלוהו - הלכך אגב אונסיה, כי א"ל: "שא קרקע זו והניחני", אקנייה ניהליה בלב שלם, וקיימא לן: "תלאו וזבין, זביניה זבינא" (ב"ב דף מז:):
Rashi on Gittin 55b:14:4.english: He should be killed - Therefore, owing to his duress, when [the owner] says to him, "Take this land and leave me [alive]," he transfers it to him wholeheartedly, and we hold [as law]: "If one hung him [in coercion] and he sold [it], his sale is a [valid] sale" (Bava Batra 47b):

Rashi on Gittin 55b:16:1.hebrew: מפחד - דואג לראות הנולד, שלא תארע תקלה בכך אם אעשה זאת:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:16:1.english: Fears - [is] concerned to foresee the outcome, so that no mishap will occur through this if I do it:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:16:2.hebrew: שקא דריספק - דופן של מרכבת נשים שקורין ריטוג"א (מרכבה (בגרמנית)) בלשון אשכנז, והיא כעין עגלה, דאמרינן באותו ואת בנו (חולין דף עט.), "כי מעיילית לי כודנייתא בריספק":
Rashi on Gittin 55b:16:2.english: A shaft of a chariot [shaka de-rispak] - The side of a women's carriage, which is called rituga [Reitwagen] (a carriage (in German)) in the language of Ashkenaz [German]; and it is like a type of wagon, as we say in [the chapter entitled] Oto veEt Beno (Chullin 79a), "When you bring me mules [hitched] to a rispak."

Rashi on Gittin 55b:16:3.english: Kamtza and bar Kamtza - Such [was] the name of two Jews:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:17:1.english: Whose friend [was] Kamtza - His friend was named Kamtza:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:1:1.hebrew: ומה טעם אמרו נודעה אינה מכפרת - דקתני מתניתין "שלא נודעה מכפרת", הא נודעה — אינה מכפרת, כלומר אינה קריבה:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:1:1.english: And what is the reason [that the Sages] said [that if] it is known, it does not effect atonement - Because the Mishnah teaches, "[If] it is not known, it effects atonement," [implying that if] it is known, it does not effect atonement — that is to say, it is not offered:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:2:1.english: This is the reason that [the Mishnah] teaches [the case of] a sin-offering - because there is eating by the priests:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:3:1.english: Since it is entirely [consumed] - and [people] will say [that] the altar consumes stolen property:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:4:1.hebrew: איפכא מיבעי ליה - למיתני: "ועל חטאת הגזולה שנודעה לרבים, שאינה מכפרת מפני תקנת המזבח":
Rashi on Gittin 55b:4:1.english: It should have [stated] the opposite - [That is, it should have taught:] "And regarding a stolen sin-offering that became known to the public, that it does not effect atonement, for the benefit of the altar":

Rashi on Gittin 55b:6:1.english: He pays double payment - because when he stole it, it was non-sacred:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:6:2.hebrew: ואינו משלם תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה - דכי טבח ומכר, הקדש הואי, ואין תשלומי כפל ותשלומי ארבעה וחמשה נוהגין בהקדש, כדילפינן בהזהב (ב"מ דף נז:):
Rashi on Gittin 55b:6:2.english: But he does not pay fourfold or fivefold payment - for when he slaughtered or sold [it], it was [already] consecrated property, and double payment and fourfold or fivefold payment do not apply to consecrated property, as we derive in [the chapter entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 57b):

Rashi on Gittin 55b:6:3.hebrew: בחוץ - אי שחט בחוץ, ענוש כרת:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:6:3.english: Outside - If he slaughtered [it] outside [the Temple], he is punishable by karet:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:6:4.hebrew: כרת מאי עבידתיה - דבשלמא לענין תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה לא קשיא לן, דאיכא למימר דכי אמר "יאוש כדי לא קני", לענין הקרבה קאמר ולא לענין הקדש קאמר; אלא כרת, אי מדאורייתא לא חזיא להקרבה, הא קיימא לן (זבחים דף קיב.): "הראוי לפתח אהל מועד" — חייבין עליו בחוץ, מידי אחרינא לא:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:6:4.english: What is the relevance of karet - Granted, with respect to fourfold and fivefold payment, it is not difficult for us, for one can say that when he said "despair alone does not acquire," he said [it] with respect to offering [it on the altar], and did not say [it] with respect to consecration. Rather, [as for] karet: if by Torah law it is not fit for offering, behold, it is established for us (Zevachim 112a): [Only] that which is fit [to be brought] to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting — one is liable for [slaughtering] it outside [the Temple], [but] anything else, not:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:7:1.hebrew: כרת שע"י דבריהם באת לו - כרת דאורייתא, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:7:1.english: Karet that comes to him through their words - [That is,] Biblical karet, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:7:2.hebrew: אוקמוה רבנן - ברשות גנב אם הקדישה, שיחול עליה הקדש גמור ושיתחייב כרת אם ישחטנה בחוץ, כי היכי דאוקמוה ברשותיה לענין כפרה; וקנס היא דקנסוהו, והפקר ב"ד הפקר הוא, וקדשה:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:7:2.english: The Sages placed it - in the thief's possession if he consecrated it, so that full consecration would take effect upon it and he would become liable for karet if he slaughters it outside [the Temple], just as they placed it in his possession with respect to atonement; and it is a penalty that they imposed upon him, for property declared ownerless by the court is ownerless, and [thus] it becomes consecrated:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:8:1.hebrew: לגיזותיה וולדותיה - דלפני הקדש, אי אמרת משעת גנבה קיימא ברשותיה, גיזותיה דידיה הוא, ואינו משלם אלא דמי פרה העומדת לילד, ולא דמי פרה וולדה:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:8:1.english: With regard to its wool and its offspring - [those from] before the consecration: if you say [that] from the time of the theft it stands in his possession, its wool is his, and he pays only the value of a cow about to give birth, and not the value of a cow and its offspring:

Rashi on Gittin 55b:9:1.hebrew: לא היה סיקריקון ביהודה - סיקריקון — עובד כוכבים רוצח, שנותן לו ישראל קרקע בפדיון נפשו, ואומר לו: "שא קרקע זו ואל תמיתני":
Rashi on Gittin 55b:9:1.english: [The law of] sikarikon did not [apply] in Judea - A sikarikon [is] a murderous idolater to whom a Jew gives land as a ransom for his life, and says to him: "Take this land and do not kill me":

Rashi on Gittin 55b:9:2.hebrew: בהרוגי המלחמה - מלחמת טיטוס שהיתה בירושלים וביהודה, ובגמ' פריך: מאי קאמר:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:9:2.english: [In the time of] those killed in the war - The war of Titus that took place in Jerusalem and in Judea; and in the Gemara it asks: What does [the Mishnah] mean?

Rashi on Gittin 55b:9:3.hebrew: מקחו בטל - דאמרי' מיראה עבד, אי נמי "השני נוח לי והראשון קשה הימנו", ובגמרא מוקי לה דלא כתב ליה שטרא:
Rashi on Gittin 55b:9:3.english: His purchase is void - for we say [the landowner] acted out of fear [of the Sicarius], or else [he reasoned], "The second [the buyer] is easy for me [to recover the land from], whereas the first [the Sicarius] is harder than him." And in the Gemara, it establishes [this ruling as applying] where [the landowner] did not write a deed [of sale] for him:

Tosafot on Gittin 55b:16:1.hebrew: אשרי אדם מפחד תמיד - בפ' הרואה (ברכות ס.) אמרינן: חזייה לההוא גברא דהוה מפחד, א"ל: חטאה את, דכתיב: "פחדו בציון חטאים", ופריך מקרא דהכא, ומוקי לה בדברי תורה, שדואג שלא ישכח תלמודו וחוזר על משנתו תמיד. והכא נמי מייתי ליה אהני עובדי, שבטחו על רוב טובתם ושלוותם לבייש את בר קמצא ולעמוד על בת קיסר, והיה להם לפחד ולדאג מן הפורענות, ולא דמי לאדם המתפחד בחנם:
Tosafot on Gittin 55b:16:1.english: Happy is the man who fears always - In the chapter [entitled] HaRoeh (Berakhot 60a), [the Gemara] says: [He] saw a certain man who was afraid; he said to him: "You are a sinner," as it is written, "Sinners in Zion are afraid." And [the Gemara] raises a difficulty from the verse here, and establishes it [as referring] to words of Torah — that he worries lest he forget his learning and reviews his mishnah always. And here too, [the Gemara] cites it regarding these incidents, where they relied on the abundance of their prosperity and their tranquility to humiliate bar Kamtza and to stand against the emperor's daughter, whereas they should have feared and worried about retribution; and it is not comparable to a person who is afraid for no reason:

Tosafot on Gittin 55b:1:1.hebrew: שלא יאמרו מזבח אוכל גזילות - וא"ת: וכי יש כח ביד חכמים לעקור דבר מן התורה בקום עשה, דמן התורה אין צריך להביא קרבן אחר? וי"ל, דדווקא נודעה קודם זריקה אינה מכפרת, אבל לאחר זריקה, שכבר נתכפר, לא הצריכוהו להביא אחרת:
Tosafot on Gittin 55b:1:1.english: So that [people] not say the altar consumes stolen property - And if you say: Do the Sages have the power to uproot a matter from the Torah by a positive action, for by Torah law he does not need to bring another offering? And one can say [in answer] that specifically [when] it became known before the sprinkling [of the blood], it does not effect atonement, but after the sprinkling [of the blood], when he has already received atonement, they did not require him to bring another [offering]:

Tosafot on Gittin 55b:7:1.hebrew: כי היכי דליחייב עלה - פירש בקונטרס דקנסוהו רבנן, וקשה, דמי לא עסקינן דאפילו שחטה אחר בחוץ דחייב? אלא, כיון דלא נודעה לרבים, אוקמוה ברשותיה שלא יהו כהנים עצבים, וממילא מחייב השוחט בחוץ:
Tosafot on Gittin 55b:7:1.english: So that he would become liable for it - Rashi explained that the Rabbis penalized him. And [this] is difficult, for are we not dealing [with a case] where even if another person slaughtered it outside [the Temple], he is liable? Rather, since [the theft] was not known to the public, [the Sages] placed it in his possession so that the priests should not be saddened, and automatically [anyone] who slaughters [it] outside [the Temple] becomes liable:

Tosafot on Gittin 55b:8:1.hebrew: לגיזותיה וולדותיה - וא"ת, אפי' קודם הקדש הן שלו, דהא תנן (ב"ק דף צג:): גזל פרה מעוברת וילדה ורחל טעונה וגזזה — משלם דמי פרה העומדת לילד ודמי רחל העומדת ליגזז; ואם נתעברה אצלו, משלם כשעת הגזלה. וי"ל דנפקא מינה לר"מ, דאמר התם בגמרא: משלם אותה ואת גיזותיה ואת ולדותיה, משום דקנסו גזלן. ואע"ג דשינוי קונה, הכא מ"מ בשעת הקדש אוקמוה ברשותיה ולא קנסו. ולרבי יהודה דאמר גזילה חוזרת בעיניה — לרב זביד דאמר אליביה שבח שעל גבי הגזילה דנגזל הוי, הכא דאוקמוה ברשותיה, דגזלן הוי; אבל לרב פפא דאמר אליביה דהוי דגזלן, לא נפקא מינה מידי. ולרבי שמעון דאמר התם למחצה ולשליש ולרביע — הכא הוי הכל שלו; אבל לרב זביד דאמר דלר"ש כוליה דגזלן, לא נפקא מינה מידי הכא במאי דאוקמוה ברשותיה:
Tosafot on Gittin 55b:8:1.english: With regard to its wool and its offspring - And if you will say: Even before consecration they are his! For we learned in a Mishnah (Bava Kamma 93b): [If] one robbed a pregnant cow and it gave birth, or a ewe laden [with wool] and he sheared it, he pays the value of a cow that is about to give birth and the value of a ewe that is about to be sheared; and if it became pregnant while in his possession, he pays as of the time of the robbery. And one can answer that there is a practical difference according to Rabbi Meir, who says there in the Gemara: He pays [for] it and its wool and its offspring, because they penalized the robber. And even though a change acquires [the stolen item], here, nevertheless, at the time of consecration they placed it in his possession, and did not penalize [him]. And according to Rabbi Yehuda, who says [that] a stolen object returns as it is — according to Rav Zevid, who says according to his view [that] the appreciation upon the stolen object belongs to the victim of the robbery, here, since they placed it in his possession, it belongs to the robber; however, according to Rav Pappa, who says according to his view that it belongs to the robber, there is no practical difference at all. And according to Rabbi Shimon, who says there [that the appreciation is divided] in half, a third, or a quarter — here all of it is his; however, according to Rav Zevid, who says that according to Rabbi Shimon all of it belongs to the robber, there is no practical difference here in that they placed it in his possession:

Tosafot on Gittin 55b:9:1.hebrew: ביהודה בהרוגי המלחמה - בירושלמי: בראשונה גזרו גזרה על יהודה, לפי שמסורת בידם מאבותם שיהודה הרג עשו, דכתיב (בראשית מט) "ידך בעורף אויביך", ותניא נמי בספרי: "ידיו רב לו" — בשעה שהרג את עשו. ובסוף פ"ק דסוטה (דף יג.), דאמר: חושים בן דן שקל קולפא ומחייה ארישיה דעשו, ונתרו עיניה ונפלו אכרעיה דיעקב — שמא לא מת באותה הכאה, עד שעמד עליו יהודה והרגו:
Tosafot on Gittin 55b:9:1.english: In Judea in [the time of] those killed in the war - In the Yerushalmi: At first they issued a decree [of persecution] against Judea, because they had a tradition from their ancestors that Judah killed Esau, as it is written (Genesis 49): "Your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies," and it is also taught in the Sifrei [regarding the verse]: "His hands contended for him" — [this was] at the time when he killed Esau. And [as for] the end of the first chapter of Sotah (13a), where it says [that] Chushim the son of Dan took a club and struck Esau on his head, and his eyes popped out and fell at Jacob's feet — perhaps he did not die from that blow, until Judah stood over him and killed him:
